main_body: Round stone well curb (rows 14-31) with a wooden roof beam, two posts and a hanging bucket above it
top_band: Light grey stone rim rows 14-16 (#c9d1d0/#9eadad) at the back, then dark water ellipse rows 17-21, then a front rim at rows 22-24
evidence: The column at x=16 shows a light back rim (rows 14-15), a dark blue water opening (rows 17-21, L about 47), a mid-tone front rim (rows 22-24), a step down to darker stone (rows 25-26), and then the stone-course front face to row 31. The ellipse of the rim and the visible water surface read as a horizontal surface seen from above, with a vertical front face below it. This matches the well and rim of the Beodeul references and the green ellipse-top guide. The roof beam is a small detail and does not change the verdict.

style.evidence: The stone ramp has about 6 lightness steps (L 206, 169, 130, 97, 71, 48), plus separate water highlights and the wood ramp on the beam. Flat-fill coverage is 0%, and the stone blocks are shaded individually. Median colours per tile is 11, against 17 and 20 for the references, and total colours is 23, against 38 and 40. That is lower but not far below. The dark edge pixels are 27% neutral, close to the well-roofed reference at 33%, so the outline is a mix of tinted and neutral. It would sit acceptably beside the reference, though somewhat plainer.
